name: Sporadic Idiopathic Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in African and Asian populations

criteria.description: Persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria despite standard corticosteroid therapy for at least 4 weeks
Renal biopsy showing minimal change disease, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, or other idiopathic glomerulopathies
Exclusion of secondary causes of nephrotic syndrome such as infections, systemic diseases, or drug-induced nephropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria unresponsive to corticosteroids for at least 4 weeks, hypoalbuminemia, and characteristic renal biopsy findings after exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be considered to exclude hereditary forms of steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome.

common.notes: Mild to moderate elevated blood pressure

rare.notes: Due to fluid overload in severe cases

rare.notes: Secondary to uremia or fluid retention

laboratory: Normal or elevated serum creatinine depending on disease progression
imaging: Renal ultrasound typically normal or shows increased echogenicity
Chest X-ray may show pleural effusions or pulmonary edema in advanced cases
genetic: Negative for known mutations in NPHS1, NPHS2, WT1 genes in idiopathic cases
Genetic testing recommended to exclude hereditary SRNS
other: Renal biopsy showing minimal change disease, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, or other idiopathic glomerulopathies

distinguishingFeatures: Onset in first 3 months of life
Poor response to steroids from birth
Associated with systemic diseases (e.g., lupus, diabetes)
Histological findings consistent with secondary causes

redFlags: Persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria despite adequate steroid therapy
